mechanism_narrative: The catastrophic collapse of RETAIL_REC to -60.4% at t-0w represents demand destruction from lockdown enforcement. Absent policy reversal, this floor persists because consumers lack permission and habit to return; retail mobility remains depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined from -14.3% to -60.4% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the prior 28 days by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility collapsed from +0.7% to -19.1% at t-0w, signaling supply-chain stress and consumer panic-buying saturation. This shift reduces incidental retail visits bundled with grocery trips, suppressing RETAIL_REC recovery over the next two weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM dropped 19.8 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 10 percentage points in the week immediately following the GROCERY_PHARM collapse.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility fell to -63.1% at t-0w, eliminating commute-anchored retail visits and weekday foot traffic. The sustained suppression of workplace presence over four weeks mechanically reduces retail-recreation mobility through loss of incidental shopping during work-adjacent hours.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -50% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers to above -30% within two weeks AND RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises by more than 15 percentage points.

The interaction of maximal residential concentration with minimal workplace presence creates a regime where retail recovery is structurally blocked for four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds +35% AND WORKPLACES falls below -60% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at +38.9% and WORKPLACES at -63.1% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -40% within the first two weeks of the forecast period despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +30%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility collapsed to -67.3% at t-0w, the deepest decline across all categories. This signals either public-transport shutdown or voluntary avoidance due to infection risk. Sustained transit suppression blocks retail access for non-car populations, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -60% in a single week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -67.3% at t-0w, the largest decline
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers to above -40% within two weeks AND RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises by more than 20 percentage points.

If parks remain closed or feared over the next four weeks, consumers lose a substitute for indoor retail leisure, but this effect is weak because parks and retail serve different demand. Retail remains depressed independent of parks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -40% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from -12.3% to -48.9% over four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS recovers to above -20% within two weeks AND RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises by more than 25 percentage points.

Consumers cannot access retail via transit and lack outdoor substitutes, creating a compounding confinement effect that suppresses retail recovery over the next two weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at +0.7% at t-1w, -19.1% at t-0w
